use_case_name: Respond to a Second-Chance Purchase Offer

claims.content: To allow the second-place finisher to accept or decline a purchase offer for an item that was previously won but cancelled due to non-payment, thereby enabling faster inventory turnover and improved customer experience.

goal.raw_text: To allow the second-place finisher to accept or decline a purchase offer for an item that was previously won but cancelled due to non-payment, thereby enabling faster inventory turnover and improved customer experience.

claims.content: Customer
An auction has ended and the winning bidder did not pay within 7 days (168 hours) of the auction ending time.
The order for the winning bidder has been cancelled and the item is placed into a 'hold' status.
A second-place finisher exists for the auctioned item.
The second-place finisher’s bid is at or above the item’s unit cost.
An automated email offering the item to the second-place finisher at their last bid price has been triggered and sent.
The customer receives an automated email offering to sell the item at their last bid price after the original winning bidder’s order was cancelled due to non-payment.

trigger.raw_text: The customer receives an automated email offering to sell the item at their last bid price after the original winning bidder’s order was cancelled due to non-payment.

claims.content: The customer receives an automated email offering to purchase the item at their last bid price, with three response options: Credit Card Option, PayPal or Amazon Payments Option, and Decline Option.
If selecting the Credit Card Option, the customer clicks 'I accept, pay with my On File credit card' button within three days of email receipt.
Clicking the Credit Card Option button triggers an automated process to generate an order and ship the item; no further action by the customer is needed.
If selecting the PayPal or Amazon Payments Option, the customer clicks 'Pay with PayPal or Amazon Payments' button within three days of email receipt.
Clicking the PayPal or Amazon Payments button generates the order and loads the Sign-In page.
After signing in, the customer is taken to the Returning Winners Payments Page where they can pay for the order.
If selecting the Decline Option, the customer clicks the 'No Thanks' button.
Clicking the 'No Thanks' button releases the item from hold status back into auction available inventory.
If the customer does not respond to the 2nd-Chance email within 72 hours after the email is sent, the item will be returned to auction available inventory and rescheduled for a future auction.
The email will not be sent if the 2nd-place finisher's bid is below the item's unit cost.
2nd-Chance emails will not be sent to recipients who have two accounts and are essentially bidding against themselves.
Before sending the email, the system should compare the 2nd-Chance recipient's account data to the Winner's account data.
The email will not be sent if matches are found on any of: Customer Name, Customer Phone Number, Customer Email Address, Customer Member ID, or Customer Billing and/or Shipping Addresses.
If the customer accepts via Credit Card Option, an order is generated and the item is shipped; no further action by the customer is needed.
If the customer accepts via PayPal or Amazon Payments Option, the order is generated and the customer pays for it on the Returning Winners Payments Page after signing in.
If the customer declines via the 'No Thanks' button, the item is released from hold status back into auction available inventory.
If the customer does not respond within 72 hours after the email is sent, the item is returned to auction available inventory and rescheduled for a future auction.

The Auction Admin’s '2nd-Chance Report' is updated to reflect: number of emails sent over the past week, number of acceptances, number of actual payments made, revenue generated from each, total revenue, total COGS, and gross margin percentage.
